title: Klippo Subcategory Prompt Variation Library
source: Additive structured library derived from prompts/prompt_component_tables.json subcategories; existing master prompts remain unchanged.
selection_policy: Select one variation for the exact selected subcategory; avoid the last three choices for that subcategory. Use category-safe actions and only reference-visible details.
global_rules: Preserve the exact visible product identity, shape, colour, pattern, labels, proportions and supplied parts.
Do not invent functions, materials, ingredients, accessories, claims, prices, discounts or results.
Keep actions physically plausible; simplify to a camera-only detail reveal if the reference does not support the action.
Do not force a human, child or animal model; follow the user's explicit model selection and model-safety rules.
No on-screen text, captions, extra logos or watermark unless the user explicitly selected text.

variations.name: Window-Light Outfit Reveal
variations.hook: Open with the full women's outfit in a softly lit room, clearly showing the actual neckline, sleeve shape, length and overall silhouette. Preserve the reference colour, print and styling exactly; no text, captions or added logos.
variations.action: The wearer steps once into the brighter part of the room and settles naturally, allowing the garment to fall into its existing shape without tugging or restyling it.
variations.detail: Show only visible design details such as the neckline, sleeve edge, waist seam or hem where present. Do not invent lining, pockets, fastenings or fabric properties.
variations.camera: Start in a medium-full frame and glide backward to a full-outfit view, keeping the same wearer and garment proportions throughout.
variations.lighting: Use broad window light with gentle fill and consistent exposure; retain natural skin tones and the garment's true colour.
variations.closing: Hold a still full-length front view with the outfit unobstructed for the final beat.
variations.audio: Use gentle modern instrumental music at low volume; no spoken claims or exaggerated transition sounds.

variations.name: Pleat and Hem Movement
variations.hook: Begin with the real hemline and any visible pleats or folds in focus, then reveal enough of the outfit to establish its full shape. Keep all visible edges and print placement faithful to the reference.
variations.action: The model takes one small sideways step and stops, letting the hem move briefly before settling; do not spin or lift the garment.
variations.detail: Highlight only the actual hem finish, pleats or folds visible in the reference. Do not add lace, trim, slits or extra layers.
variations.camera: Tilt smoothly from the lower garment to a balanced full-length frame, with no whip-pan and no cropping of the hem.
variations.lighting: Use soft diffused light with a natural floor shadow, preserving detail in both light and dark fabric.
variations.closing: End on a full-length still frame once the hem has settled.
variations.audio: A faint fabric rustle is appropriate only if the movement supports it; keep music restrained.

variations.name: Neckline and Shoulder Study
variations.hook: Open on the real neckline and shoulder line, then widen to show how those details connect to the complete outfit. Preserve the exact collar shape, sleeve attachment and any visible fastening.
variations.action: The wearer gently turns their upper body a few degrees and returns to front, keeping hands away from the neckline.
variations.detail: Show only visible neckline edges, seams or fastenings that exist; do not add jewellery, buttons or decorative stitching.
variations.camera: Use a stable close-to-medium composition followed by a slow pullback to a medium-full frame; avoid lens distortion.
variations.lighting: Soft off-axis light defines the shoulder and neckline without shifting colour or creating artificial shine.
variations.closing: Finish with the neckline and most of the outfit visible in a steady front-facing pose.
variations.audio: Use clean low-volume instrumental music; no handling sounds because the wearer does not touch the garment.

variations.name: Pattern Placement Walk-By
variations.hook: Show the outfit front-on first so its actual print, motifs or colour blocking can be read. Do not create extra symbols, text or branding, and keep the pattern's scale consistent.
variations.action: The model walks two calm steps across the frame and stops in a slight three-quarter pose; movement remains gentle enough to preserve pattern continuity.
variations.detail: Focus on the genuine placement of the print across visible panels. Do not mirror motifs, change their spacing or claim anything about fabric quality.
variations.camera: Track laterally at a steady distance with the full outfit in frame; avoid a fast orbit or sudden zoom.
variations.lighting: Use even daylight with stable white balance so the print does not change colour between frames.
variations.closing: Hold the three-quarter pose, then settle into a clean view with the key print area unobstructed.
variations.audio: Choose a light rhythmic instrumental bed; footsteps only if they match the visible surface.

variations.name: Flat-Lay to Worn Cut
variations.hook: If the supplied reference includes a flat-lay or hanging view, begin with that exact garment and transition by a clean cut to the same item worn; otherwise keep the original setup and do a camera-only reveal. No added props or text.
variations.action: Use one simple cut between compatible views; do not morph the garment or invent a dressing action.
variations.detail: Maintain the same colour, pattern, visible seams, sleeve shape and hem in both views. Do not add accessories or hidden construction.
variations.camera: Use two similarly composed shots with a clean cut and stable scale; no shape-distorting transition.
variations.lighting: Match the light direction and colour balance across both shots to keep the product identity consistent.
variations.closing: Hold the complete worn outfit or original presentation in a clear final frame, depending on the reference.
variations.audio: A soft music beat may mark the cut; no magical transformation sound or spoken claims.

variations.name: Natural Drape in a Still Pose
variations.hook: Present the complete outfit against a plain, quiet background before movement starts, allowing its true cut and drape to register. Keep the reference styling unchanged.
variations.action: The wearer shifts weight once and relaxes their shoulders; no wind, dramatic swaying or deliberate reshaping of the garment.
variations.detail: Show the actual folds and silhouette only. Do not assert softness, breathability, stretch, wrinkle resistance or any unverified fabric feature.
variations.camera: Keep the camera almost locked, with a very slow straight push-in that retains the garment's defining outline.
variations.lighting: Use broad diffused light and subtle shadow gradients so folds remain visible without altering colour.
variations.closing: Stop the camera and hold the outfit still in a full or medium-full view.
variations.audio: Use a quiet instrumental bed; avoid artificial wind or fabric effects.

variations.name: Sleeve Detail to Full Look
variations.hook: Begin close on a real sleeve cuff, sleeve edge or visible sleeve pattern, then reveal the complete outfit. Keep the sleeve length, shape and pattern unchanged.
variations.action: The model lowers one arm naturally from a relaxed bent position to their side, then becomes still.
variations.detail: Feature only the visible cuff, seam and sleeve drape; do not invent buttons, thumb loops, embroidery or special fabric performance.
variations.camera: Start with a steady close detail and pull back continuously to a medium-full composition, keeping the garment centred.
variations.lighting: Use soft side light to define the sleeve edge while retaining natural skin tone and true garment colour.
variations.closing: End with the sleeve unobstructed and enough of the outfit visible to identify the full design.
variations.audio: Keep music soft; a small fabric rustle is optional only if the arm movement plausibly produces it.

variations.name: Front-to-Profile Fit Check
variations.hook: Open with the complete outfit facing forward so its real fit and proportions are clear. Maintain the same wearer, hairstyle, accessories already present and garment details throughout.
variations.action: The model turns slowly to a three-quarter angle, pauses, and returns to front without spinning or changing pose dramatically.
variations.detail: Use the angle change to show only the visible side silhouette and seams; do not reveal imagined back details or reshape the waist or hem.
variations.camera: Use a level full-length shot and a very small camera arc that complements the turn without passing behind the model.
variations.lighting: Keep broad soft lighting consistent across both angles so colour and shadows remain believable.
variations.closing: Return to the opening front view and hold it still with the whole outfit visible.
variations.audio: Use understated fashion music with no runway crowd, applause or unsupported sound effects.

variations.name: Seated Detail, Standing Silhouette
variations.hook: If the reference outfit can naturally be shown seated, open with the wearer seated upright and the garment clearly visible; otherwise begin in a relaxed standing pose. Do not force a pose that hides or distorts the product.
variations.action: When seated, the model rises slowly in one continuous movement and stands still; when standing is the only suitable setup, they simply shift weight once.
variations.detail: Show how the existing garment settles after the movement without implying a guaranteed fit, comfort or suitability for other body types.
variations.camera: Use a fixed medium-wide frame with enough space for the full movement; avoid cuts during the rise and keep the hem inside frame.
variations.lighting: Maintain even soft light throughout the action to prevent changes in fabric shade or exposure.
variations.closing: Hold a relaxed full-outfit front view once the model is still.
variations.audio: Use gentle instrumental music and subtle room tone; no dramatic rise sound or spoken product claims.

variations.name: Editorial Full-Length Finish
variations.hook: Start with the entire outfit in a clean, uncluttered setting; use negative space from the background rather than adding props or graphics. Keep the product's actual cut, colour and print unchanged.
variations.action: The wearer takes one measured step toward a natural final mark and settles into a relaxed pose with hands clear of key details.
variations.detail: Allow the real silhouette, visible seams and hem to carry the shot. Do not imply occasion suitability or unverified material and quality claims.
variations.camera: Begin slightly wider to establish the setting, then make one slow straight push-in that ends with the complete outfit still inside frame.
variations.lighting: Use soft neutral light with gentle contrast; no artificial glow, dramatic colour grade or shifting highlights.
variations.closing: Finish on a steady, full-length hero frame with the wearer centred and the garment unobstructed.
variations.audio: Use polished but unobtrusive instrumental music beneath any selected narration; no added words or exaggerated effects.

variations.name: Tailored Front-to-Profile
variations.hook: Open on the men's garment worn or displayed straight-on, with its real neckline, shoulder line and overall silhouette immediately legible; keep the reference item unchanged and show no text or added branding.
variations.action: The model eases into a three-quarter stance, pauses long enough to read the side silhouette, then returns to face front in one controlled movement.
variations.detail: Let the change of angle reveal only construction that is actually visible, such as the collar, sleeve opening or hem; do not imply hidden pockets, stretch, lining or fabric performance.
variations.camera: Frame from head to mid-thigh or wide enough to include the whole garment, then make a slow, level arc of only a few degrees rather than circling the wearer.
variations.lighting: Use a broad soft key and gentle fill so dark and light areas retain detail without shifting the garment's true colour.
variations.closing: Settle into a straight-on full-garment frame and hold it still for the final beat, with hands clear of the main design.
variations.audio: Use restrained contemporary instrumental music beneath any selected voice; no whooshes or spoken product claims.

variations.name: Cuff-to-Silhouette Story
variations.hook: Begin close on a visible sleeve cuff or sleeve edge, then establish that detail as part of the complete men's garment; preserve the exact colour, pattern and proportions from the reference.
variations.action: The wearer lowers an arm naturally from a relaxed bent position to their side, allowing the sleeve to fall into place without pulling or reshaping it.
variations.detail: Keep attention on the actual cuff, seam and sleeve drape only where the reference shows them; never invent buttons, stitching or premium-material claims.
variations.camera: Start with a steady close detail, then pull back in one continuous move to a medium-full composition with the garment still centred.
variations.lighting: Use soft side light to create enough tonal separation to read the sleeve edge while keeping shadows open and realistic.
variations.closing: Hold the final composition with the sleeve unobstructed and the rest of the garment clearly identifiable.
variations.audio: A faint fabric rustle is suitable only if audible handling is visible; keep music quiet and avoid artificial transition effects.

variations.name: Walk-In Natural Fit
variations.hook: Show the complete men's outfit in a believable everyday setting with a clear view of its real fit before the movement begins; add no props that suggest features or uses not shown.
variations.action: The model takes two measured steps toward the camera, stops comfortably, and lets the garment settle without exaggerated posing or a fast turn.
variations.detail: Use the natural movement to show how the existing cut hangs in motion, without claiming breathability, stretch, comfort or any other unverified performance.
variations.camera: Track backward smoothly at the model's pace, maintaining a consistent distance and keeping the garment within frame without a sudden zoom.
variations.lighting: Choose soft open-shade or window-like daylight with consistent exposure as the model approaches; keep colour and skin tone natural.
variations.closing: End with the wearer stationary in a relaxed front-facing stance and the whole outfit visible for a clean product hold.
variations.audio: Pair low-volume lifestyle music with clear selected speech if present; avoid footsteps unless they fit the visible surface and scene.

variations.name: Flat-Lay Construction Tour
variations.hook: Present the men's garment neatly arranged on a plain surface, with the full outline visible before the camera explores its real construction; no extra accessories or on-screen text.
variations.action: Keep the item still and let the viewer discover it through camera movement alone; do not animate, stretch or rearrange the garment.
variations.detail: Travel across visible elements such as collar shape, front opening, print placement or hem, selecting only features genuinely present in the supplied image.
variations.camera: Use a controlled overhead glide from the upper section toward the lower section, then settle into a full-item overhead view; avoid extreme macro that distorts texture.
variations.lighting: Use broad diffused light from one side with soft contact shadows, preventing glare and preserving the garment's actual shade.
variations.closing: Finish on the complete flat-lay, aligned neatly in frame with no cropped edges.
variations.audio: Choose minimal instrumental music; no handling sounds should be added while the garment remains untouched.

variations.name: Layering Without Restyling
variations.hook: Open with the men's outer layer or top as supplied, fully readable against a simple background; keep every visible layer exactly as shown in the reference.
variations.action: The wearer makes one small shoulder turn and returns to centre, allowing the existing layers to separate visually through natural movement without adding or removing anything.
variations.detail: Show only the real overlap, neckline and hem relationships visible in the outfit; do not invent pockets, fasteners or extra garments.
variations.camera: Use a locked medium-full shot with a gentle reframing adjustment only if needed to keep the full silhouette inside the frame.
variations.lighting: Use balanced studio-style light with subtle side definition, avoiding dramatic shadows that hide the garment's edges.
variations.closing: Hold the original front view with the layers settled and all key visible parts unobstructed.
variations.audio: Use understated fashion-showcase music without a runway crowd or applause unless the setting actually depicts one.

variations.name: Fabric Movement in Profile
variations.hook: Start from a clean side view of the men's garment so its real outline is easy to read; the opening should feel like an observational product film, not a claim about the fabric.
variations.action: The wearer shifts weight once from one foot to the other and returns to a balanced stance, creating only the natural movement caused by that shift.
variations.detail: Observe the actual folds and drape as they change, but do not describe the fabric as soft, lightweight, waterproof or wrinkle-free unless verified separately.
variations.camera: Hold a level profile medium shot, then make a small, smooth move toward a three-quarter angle without passing behind the wearer.
variations.lighting: Keep a broad soft source consistent through the movement so folds remain visible and the colour does not fluctuate.
variations.closing: Stop the movement and hold the three-quarter view long enough to inspect the garment's real shape.
variations.audio: Use a quiet, steady instrumental bed; avoid dramatic swells or sound effects that imply a transformation.

variations.name: Collar and Neckline Reveal
variations.hook: Open with the garment's actual neckline or collar in crisp focus, then make the wider men's garment clear before the shot ends; preserve the exact collar shape and fastening details.
variations.action: The model gently turns the head and upper body a little to one side, then faces forward again, keeping hands away from the neckline.
variations.detail: Show only the collar edge, neckline and any visible fastening that exists in the reference; do not add buttons, tags or stitching that cannot be seen.
variations.camera: Use a stable close-to-medium framing and a gradual pullback, with no artificial focus breathing or exaggerated lens distortion.
variations.lighting: Place soft light slightly off-axis to define the neckline without creating harsh glare or altering the product's colour.
variations.closing: Finish with the collar and full upper garment both readable in a steady medium shot.
variations.audio: Keep the soundtrack clean and low; omit handling sounds because the model does not touch the garment.

variations.name: Seated-to-Standing Continuity
variations.hook: Begin with the men's garment visible in a natural seated pose, only if that pose suits the supplied outfit and reference; keep the product and styling consistent from the first frame.
variations.action: The model rises slowly to a comfortable standing position in one continuous motion, without pulling at the hem or changing any garment details.
variations.detail: Let the camera reveal the actual way the garment settles after standing; do not imply hidden construction or promise a fit result for other body types.
variations.camera: Use a fixed, level medium-wide frame that has enough headroom and lower-body space for the complete movement; avoid cuts during the rise.
variations.lighting: Maintain even, soft light through the entire action so the garment does not change shade between poses.
variations.closing: Once standing, pause in a relaxed front-facing position with the full garment visible and still.
variations.audio: Use a subtle instrumental track and natural room tone; do not add a dramatic rise sound or voiceover claims.

variations.name: Print and Pattern Read
variations.hook: Reveal the men's garment against a quiet, uncluttered background, opening close enough to read its visible print or surface pattern before showing the whole item.
variations.action: The wearer makes a small, slow quarter-turn and returns to the starting angle so the existing pattern can be seen from a second view without spinning.
variations.detail: Keep print scale, alignment and colour consistent with the reference; do not generate extra motifs, mirrored logos or invented texture.
variations.camera: Make a restrained lateral slide parallel to the garment, then stop in a straight, medium-full frame; keep the camera movement independent of the model's turn.
variations.lighting: Use broad, even light to avoid hotspots and preserve pattern contrast without sharpening the surface into a false texture.
variations.closing: Hold the clearest front view with the print unobstructed and the garment fully recognizable.
variations.audio: Choose simple mid-tempo instrumental music at low volume; no sound effects are needed for a camera slide.

variations.name: Still Pose, Slow Push
variations.hook: Show the complete men's garment in a composed hero frame, then draw the viewer closer through a measured camera move rather than a dramatic model pose.
variations.action: The wearer remains relaxed, making only a small natural breath and posture adjustment; no spinning, walking or garment tugging.
variations.detail: As the camera moves closer, emphasize visible fit lines, neckline, sleeve shape and hem only where those details appear in the reference.
variations.camera: Make one slow, straight push-in from a full to medium-full shot; do not orbit, jump cuts, or reveal unseen sides.
variations.lighting: Use soft frontal fill and gentle side definition, preserving realistic texture and accurate colour without adding sparkle or shine.
variations.closing: Stop before any part of the garment is cropped and hold a sharp, calm final frame.
variations.audio: Keep a minimal instrumental bed below any selected voice; avoid synthetic whooshes and unsupported spoken claims.

variations.name: Full-Length Flow Reveal
variations.hook: Open on the complete dress or robe from neckline to hem, making its real length and silhouette immediately clear. Preserve the reference colour, print and construction; no text or added branding.
variations.action: The wearer takes one slow step forward and settles, letting the existing garment move naturally without lifting or reshaping the hem.
variations.detail: Show only visible features such as sleeve shape, waist line, neckline and hem; do not invent slits, lining, pockets, fastenings or fabric properties.
variations.camera: Use a stable full-length frame, then make a subtle push-in that never crops the hem or top of the garment.
variations.lighting: Use soft, even front and side light so the garment's true shade and printed details remain accurate.
variations.closing: End in a still full-length front view with the entire garment unobstructed.
variations.audio: Use gentle instrumental music below any selected voice; no dramatic whoosh or spoken quality claims.

variations.name: Hemline in Motion
variations.hook: Begin close on the real hemline, then reveal the complete dress so the detail is understood in context; do not alter the garment's length or edge.
variations.action: The model steps slightly sideways and rests, creating a small, plausible movement through the hem rather than a spin.
variations.detail: Keep hem shape, trim and stitching faithful to the reference; never add lace, pleats or edging that is not present.
variations.camera: Start low enough to see the hem, then tilt up smoothly to a balanced full-length composition without a whip movement.
variations.lighting: Use diffused light and a soft floor shadow; retain detail in both dark fabric and light-coloured hems.
variations.closing: Hold a full-length view after the fabric settles, with the bottom edge completely inside frame.
variations.audio: A quiet fabric rustle may accompany visible movement; keep music minimal and avoid extra effects.

variations.name: Sleeve and Bodice Detail
variations.hook: Open on the dress's visible sleeve and bodice, then ease out to show how those details belong to the full silhouette; preserve seams and proportions.
variations.action: The wearer turns the upper body a few degrees and returns to centre, keeping hands away from the garment's key details.
variations.detail: Highlight only the actual sleeve cut, neckline and bodice structure shown; do not claim shaping, support or special tailoring.
variations.camera: Use a slow close-to-medium pullback with steady focus and no exaggerated macro distortion.
variations.lighting: Place soft side light to reveal edges and folds without making the fabric appear shinier or more textured than shown.
variations.closing: Finish with the upper garment and enough of the lower section visible to understand the design.
variations.audio: Use low-volume instrumental music; omit handling sounds because the model does not touch the fabric.

variations.name: Gentle Three-Quarter Turn
variations.hook: Show the entire dress in a clean front-facing frame before inviting a second view; keep wearer, garment, styling and background consistent.
variations.action: The model turns slowly to a three-quarter angle, pauses, and returns to front without spinning or leaving frame.
variations.detail: Show only real visible differences in cut and drape; do not reveal imagined back details or hidden closures.
variations.camera: Keep a level full-length shot and allow a restrained camera slide to complement, not compete with, the turn.
variations.lighting: Use balanced soft lighting so the garment colour remains consistent as its angle changes.
variations.closing: Return to the original front-facing stance and hold a clear full-length hero frame.
variations.audio: Choose calm fashion music with no runway crowd, applause or unsupported effects.

variations.name: Fold-to-Worn Match
variations.hook: Begin with the dress neatly laid out or hanging only if that matches the reference, then transition to the same garment worn by a model without changing its design.
variations.action: Use one clean cut between the views; maintain garment identity, colour, pattern and visible construction on both sides.
variations.detail: Show only features verifiable in both views; do not create extra buttons, ties, belts or accessories.
variations.camera: Use two simple, similarly framed compositions and a clean cut rather than a morph that distorts the dress.
variations.lighting: Match light direction and colour balance across both shots to reduce discontinuity.
variations.closing: Hold on the complete worn view with the full length visible and no added styling pieces.
variations.audio: Use a soft musical beat to support the cut; no transformation sound or spoken claims.

variations.name: Fabric Drape in Stillness
variations.hook: Open with the dress in a quiet full-length pose, letting its real folds and silhouette register before movement begins.
variations.action: The wearer shifts weight once, allowing only natural folds to move; no wind or exaggerated swaying.
variations.detail: Describe visible drape without asserting that the material is lightweight, stretchy, cooling or wrinkle-resistant unless verified independently.
variations.camera: Keep the camera nearly locked, then make a slow straight push toward a medium-full view without orbiting.
variations.lighting: Use broad diffused illumination with subtle shadow gradients to keep folds legible and colour true.
variations.closing: Stop before cropping the garment's defining outline and hold the still frame for inspection.
variations.audio: Use a restrained ambient instrumental bed and no artificial fabric or wind effects.

variations.name: Neckline-to-Full Look
variations.hook: Start close on the actual neckline and shoulder area, then widen to establish the complete dress or robe; keep neckline geometry as shown.
variations.action: The wearer turns their head slightly and relaxes into a neutral pose without touching or pulling the neckline.
variations.detail: Reveal only visible neckline edges, collar details or fastenings that exist; do not add jewellery or trim.
variations.camera: Pull back smoothly from a stable upper-body close-up to a full-length view, keeping the wearer centred.
variations.lighting: Use soft frontal fill and gentle side definition; avoid glare and preserve the garment's original tone.
variations.closing: Hold a final front view with neckline and hem both visible in the composition.
variations.audio: Keep music soft and clean; no touch sounds or unsupported voiceover claims.

variations.name: Side Profile and Return
variations.hook: Open on a side profile that makes the dress silhouette visible from shoulder through hem, without hiding it behind props.
variations.action: The model rotates gently from side profile to three-quarter view and stops; avoid a full turn if the reference does not support a reverse view.
variations.detail: Show only the side outline and visible seams; do not invent a train, side slit, pockets or back design.
variations.camera: Use a fixed full-length angle with a slight lateral adjustment, avoiding an orbit that reveals unseen surfaces.
variations.lighting: Use even neutral light with a soft side highlight to separate the garment from the background.
variations.closing: Finish at a three-quarter angle with the full hem in frame and the wearer motionless.
variations.audio: Use low-key instrumental music without transition accents; keep selected speech intelligible.

variations.name: Pattern Placement Showcase
variations.hook: Reveal the dress's real print at a readable distance before widening to show how it sits across the garment; preserve motif scale and placement.
variations.action: The wearer makes a small quarter-turn and returns to front so the pattern is seen from another angle without spinning.
variations.detail: Keep motifs, colours and relative positions consistent; do not generate new symbols, repeated logos or altered print alignment.
variations.camera: Make a gentle lateral slide parallel to the front, then stop in a straight full-length frame.
variations.lighting: Use broad even lighting to avoid hotspots that wash out the print or create false texture.
variations.closing: Hold the clearest front view with pattern and full silhouette unobstructed.
variations.audio: Choose simple instrumental music at low volume; no sound effects are needed for a camera move.

variations.name: Quiet Editorial Finish
variations.hook: Start with the complete dress or robe in a calm, uncluttered setting; focus on its real silhouette and colour instead of decorative props.
variations.action: The wearer takes one small step into a comfortable pose and becomes still, without gestures that hide the garment.
variations.detail: Show only visible cut, drape, sleeve and hem details; do not imply occasion suitability or performance claims.
variations.camera: Begin with modest environmental space and make one slow straight push-in ending at a medium-full frame that retains the outline.
variations.lighting: Use natural-looking consistent light and gentle contrast; no colour shift or artificial glow.
variations.closing: End with the wearer centred and relaxed, the garment clearly recognizable for the final beat.
variations.audio: Use soft modern instrumental music under selected narration; no on-screen words, added logo or exaggerated effects.

variations.name: Trackside Full-Kit Reveal
variations.hook: Open on the complete sportswear outfit in a clean, realistic training setting, with the actual cut, colour blocks, seams and visible logos exactly matching the reference. Keep the frame free of added text, badges or branding.
variations.action: The athlete stands at rest, then takes two easy warm-up steps forward and stops; the movement stays casual and does not become a strenuous performance demonstration.
variations.detail: Let the natural shift show the real fit and folds of the visible top, shorts, leggings or tracksuit. Do not claim sweat-wicking, compression, stretch, breathability or technical fabric properties unless independently verified.
variations.camera: Track backward smoothly at walking pace in a level medium-full or full-body frame, keeping the whole outfit in view and avoiding a dramatic orbit.
variations.lighting: Use soft outdoor daylight or open shade with stable exposure; preserve the reference colours and readable dark fabric detail.
variations.closing: Hold a front-facing full-outfit frame after the athlete stops, with hands away from key design areas and the garment settled.
variations.audio: Use a restrained upbeat instrumental beat under any selected narration; add footsteps only if they suit the visible ground and action.

variations.name: Lace-and-Fit Detail
variations.hook: Begin on the shoe area only if footwear is part of the supplied sportswear reference; otherwise open on a visible waistband, cuff or fastening of the garment. Keep every feature faithful to the reference and add no text.
variations.action: If the selected detail is a lace or fastening, the wearer makes one small, plausible adjustment and releases it; if it is clothing, they simply lower the arm or settle into a neutral stance without changing the fit.
variations.detail: Show only the fastening, cuff, seam or waistband that can actually be seen. Do not invent drawstrings, pockets, reflective panels, logos or performance benefits.
variations.camera: Use a steady close shot for the real detail, then pull back in one continuous move to identify the full sportswear item; do not crop in a way that implies a different product.
variations.lighting: Soft side lighting should define the edge and stitching without glare or a shift in product colour.
variations.closing: Finish with the detail unobstructed and enough of the item visible to make its context clear.
variations.audio: Keep music quiet; include a small fabric or lace sound only if the handling is visible and the sound is natural.

variations.name: Warm-Up Side Profile
variations.hook: Show the complete sportswear silhouette from a three-quarter side angle before movement begins; preserve the model, fit, pattern and styling from the reference.
variations.action: The athlete performs one gentle side step, returns to the original mark and stands relaxed. Avoid jumps, sprinting or athletic feats that are unnecessary for a product showcase.
variations.detail: Capture the genuine way the garment moves around the knees, elbows or waist during the step. Do not exaggerate stretch or imply support, protection or improved performance.
variations.camera: Keep a stable medium-wide frame and make a small lateral tracking move parallel to the athlete, never circling behind them or revealing unseen garment surfaces.
variations.lighting: Use even daylight with soft shadows and consistent white balance throughout the step.
variations.closing: Return to the same three-quarter pose and hold the full silhouette still for the final beat.
variations.audio: Choose a light training-style instrumental rhythm at low volume; no crowd, whistle or gym sounds unless the scene shows their source.

variations.name: Flat-Lay Kit Inspection
